text: Autopsy report, Vienna 1902: Subject died of temporal displacement syndrome. Internal organs aged at different rates heart from 1902, lungs from 1847, liver from 1923. Coroner noted patient was still breathing during examination.

Archaeological report: Pleistocene site, 40,000 BCE, contains Neanderthal burial with grave goods including obsidian blade, mammoth ivory, and laminated employee ID badge from Blockbuster Video. Badge expires 2004.

Personal diary, merchant's widow, Lübeck 1456: The stars rearranged themselves to spell my late husband's name. Lasted three nights. Astronomers insist no such configuration occurred. I have witnesses.

Botanical survey, Amazon basin 1889: Vine specimens collected exhibited temporal growth rings spanning centuries within hours. Pressed samples aged backward in herbarium. Original collector found saplings he planted had become ancient trees
Shipping manifest, Port of Bristol 1672: Cargo listed as 400 barrels of tomorrow's regret, properly aged. Vessel never departed. Barrels found empty in warehouse cellar 1981, still weeping.
Census data, Rome 73 CE: Population count includes 847 citizens listed as temporarily deceased. Tax records show they continued paying property levies. Burial registry has no corresponding entries.

Meteorological station log, Manitoba 1923: Blizzard deposited snow that fell upward when disturbed. Children reported building snowmen that dissolved into sky. Weather service classified incident as clerical error.

Geological survey, Precambrian shield formation 1.8 billion BCE: Rock strata contain fossilized prayers in language that won't evolve for another billion years. Text requests patience with the long waiting.

Medical records, St. Bartholomew's Hospital 1348: Patient treated for wounds sustained in battle that occurred three centuries later. Bandages bore coat of arms not yet designed. Recovery was complete.
Astronomical observation log, Beijing 1054 CE: Supernova recorded lasting 23 days. Modern telescopic analysis confirms explosion occurred in 1887. Light arrived 833 years early. No explanation filed.
Navigation charts, Caribbean 1692: Pirate vessel documented sailing through island that cartographers confirm never existed. Crew sold authentic treasures from nonexistent raids. Gold tested genuine.

Archaeological excavation, Mesopotamia 2400 BCE: USB drive recovered with cuneiform adapter still attached. Device contains 47 terabytes of data in protoAkkadian. Last accessed folder: BackupTimeline7.
Botanical survey 1789: Specimen pressed between herbarium pages shows autumn foliage collected in June. Leaves change seasons when observed directly. Botanist's notes end midsentence.
Dental records, Berlin 1923: Patient's wisdom teeth contain miniature engravings of events from 1956. Dentist's Xrays show the etchings glowing. Patient born in 1901, died in 1954.
Seismic monitoring station reports earthquake in Nevada, 1962. No structural damage recorded. Tremors spelled out HELP in Morse code across seventeen different instruments. Station was unmanned.
